create.title: Order-J Farey stationary bound for low product-wavelet conductors
create.statement_tex: Let J=sqrt(X), Q=X^(1/5), T=J/Q, and let D_C be the exact fixed-smooth-interior product-wavelet contribution from order-J Farey denominators c asymp C. Retain the two offset-Poisson aliases, X=N+vartheta, the exact neighbor-dependent half-open Farey interval, the one-sided ratio symbol, all three odd/even local residue classes, and both surviving axes. After x=Ju, y=Jv, tau=beta J^2, and tau=(J/c)z, the exact phase is (J/c){z(uv-1)-rho u-(c/[c,4])sigma v}. Every compatible nonaxial critical point is nondegenerate; the d tau measure and three-dimensional stationary phase give (c/J)^(1/2)|rho sigma|^(-1/4), with the bounded neighbor-dependent incomplete-Fresnel factor at entry and exit. The nonstationary dual tails are summable by u- or v-integration by parts, and the odd-c rho=0 and 4|c sigma=0 axes have no triple critical point. Hence D_C <<_epsilon X^epsilon C^(3/2)J^(-1/2). In particular every T<=C<=J^(2/3), equivalently X^(3/10)<=C<=X^(1/3) at the benchmark, is J^(1/2)X^epsilon-safe. This is a fixed-interior conductor-block lemma and gives no estimate for J^(2/3)<C<=J, cone edges, M9-M1, or the exponent.
create.next_action: Use this lemma only to remove T<=C<=J^(2/3). Prove signed cancellation for J^(2/3)<C<=J with sharp transitions, both even classes, and upper-conductor axial terms retained.

create.title: Upper-conductor reciprocal-square B-process self-return
create.statement_tex: On an odd-modulus nonaxial interior saddle of the order-J Farey transform, put k=rho sigma, q=4b, and A_b=(sqrt(bX)+sqrt(k)/(2sqrt(b)))^2. The exact leading arithmetic phase is e_q(k cbar)e(-A_b/c). Poisson summation in c modulo q gives q^(-1) sum_n S(n,k;q) int W(x/C)e(-A_b/x-nx/q)dx, with stationary n asymp qA_b/C^2 asymp Q^2 and critical phase -J sqrt(n)-sqrt(kn)/(2b). Expanding S(n,k;q) and applying the matching B-process in n has h asymp C and Legendre value -A_b/h; after renaming h=c it restores e_q(k cbar)e(-A_b/c), with adjoint stationary amplitudes. Thus a bare c-Poisson followed by the n-B-process is a self-return and supplies no upper-conductor saving. This statement is scoped to the smooth odd nonaxial stationary main; even classes, axes, transitions, and the required signed upper-conductor estimate remain open.
create.next_action: Do not repeat the one-variable c-Poisson/n-B-process loop. Seek genuinely joint cancellation in b and c, or a phase-specific spectral estimate that retains the square-root chirp.

Low order-J conductors through C=J^(2/3) are target-safe. Prove the upper-conductor signed reciprocal-square sum for J^(2/3)<C<=J, or find a non-self-returning joint transform; no one-variable completion or B-process repetition.
The low Farey conductors are closed, but the upper reciprocal-square transform returns under a second B-process. Attack the remaining upper conductors jointly in b and c.
